policy.relationship: Claude and Codex artifacts are peer implementations of shared agent behavior. Neither side is the canonical source; each side may be edited first.
policy.maintenance: When one side changes, the active agent must update the counterpart in the same session. Hooks remind immediately and block one-sided commits unless the changed artifact is synchronized or this manifest records an explicit artifact-specific status or exemption.

hooks.name: block-destructive-command.sh
hooks.note: Codex registers this script directly; Claude inlines the same logic in pretooluse-bash.sh so its Bash matcher emits one decision. Change and test both implementations together. Decisions are allow or deny, never approval prompts; ALLOW_CLONE=1 is the narrow clone override. Codex normalizes supported shell-tool payloads with lib-codex-hook-json.sh. Operational details live in both hook READMEs.
hooks.equivalence: Identical apart from the payload-normalization preamble; Claude's live behaviour comes from the inlined copy in pretooluse-bash.sh, not from this file.

hooks.name: block-dirty-tree-rewrite.sh
hooks.note: Blocks filter-repo and filter-branch only when the resolved target has staged or unstaged tracked changes; untracked files are deliberately ignored. Resolution uses git -C, then the last applicable cd, then the hook cwd. Heredoc bodies are masked, and ALLOW_DIRTY_REWRITE=1 is the explicit override. Codex normalizes supported shell-tool payloads; the scripts are otherwise paired. Details live in both hook READMEs.
hooks.equivalence: Identical apart from the payload-normalization preamble documented above.

hooks.name: lib-codex-hook-json.sh
hooks.note: Codex-only hook payload normalizer for tool_input/tool_response object-or-string variants. Its non-evaluating functions.exec parser emits literal nested commands and paired command/workdir records from actual tools.exec_command calls, rejects overridable object fields as ambiguous, and classifies commit syntax without treating inert quoted text as a command; Claude has no functions.exec wrapper and reads native Claude payloads directly.

hooks.name: pretooluse-bash.sh
hooks.note: Claude Bash PreToolUse dispatcher registered in ~/.claude/settings.json. It ports cheap Bash guards in-process and delegates heavier git/filesystem checks, including the GitHub write guard, to their standalone hook scripts. Its Bash command rewrite emits the full original tool_input with only command replaced so Claude's replacement-style updatedInput preserves timeout/run_in_background. Codex registers the corresponding shell hooks directly in codex/hooks.json instead of using this dispatcher and has no Bash command-rewrite counterpart.

hooks.name: wrap-bash-output.sh

hooks.name: cr-skill-routing-reminder.sh

hooks.name: cr-card-body-gate.sh
hooks.note: Claude PreToolUse Bash gate: denies a GitHub issue create/edit command when its --body-file is a CR card attempt that fails cr_card_body.py check (missing biblio/author/abstract), forcing CR cards through the template tool. Scoped to CR-card bodies; no Codex peer.

hooks.name: cr-issue-comment-freshness.sh
hooks.note: Claude-only PreToolUse gate registered in each reasoning-tasks worktree's untracked settings.local.json. It blocks issue-comment posting when a newer comment has not been acknowledged, includes the newest comment in the denial, and intentionally fails open on API errors. Codex posting is routed to Claude. Details live in claude/hooks/README.org.

Stop forwards turn-end state to Emacs, while session-learning capture belongs to the Emacs agent-before-exit path because Stop is not true process exit. Ahrefs and GitHub guard registration is documented in claude/hooks/README.org.

Tracked global registration, live through ~/.codex/hooks.json; it stays outside repo-root .codex to avoid double loading. Lifecycle entries use codex-hook-wrapper with an explicit Emacs socket. Shell matchers cover Bash, exec_command, functions.exec, and functions.exec_command; edit matchers are collapsed for trust review, and UserPromptSubmit has an empty matcher. Guards allow or deny, never ask. The Drive runtime-state guard was removed on 2026-08-03 with the rest of the Drive workspace tooling, so its shell-matcher entry is gone. See codex/README.org and codex/hooks/README.org.

Shared deny-by-default allowlist for agent-initiated GitHub writes. Claude and Codex guards block git push and mutating gh operations unless the target repo matches an exact OWNER/REPO entry or OWNER/* account wildcard here. The benthamite/* entry permits repositories in Pablo's GitHub account; other entries should cover only repositories or accounts Pablo explicitly authorizes.

Tracked global config, live through ~/.codex/config.toml. Codex-only trust, plugin, theme, app, MCP, account, and model state has no Claude counterpart; project-doc fallbacks remain disabled and [features].hooks enables hooks. bin/skill-prune owns managed [[skills.config]] entries and shared disable state. bin/codex-config-prune removes dead project and hook-trust records. Moving a repository means rewriting its [projects."..."] trust key and merging it with any entry Codex appended for the new path; a duplicate table makes the config unparseable. See codex/README.org.

Ensures the live ~/.codex/skills directory is a symlink to the tracked codex/skills tree because Codex discovers global skills from ~/.codex/skills/*/SKILL.md. Also installs local gitignored private-skill shims from the encrypted private manifest.

Creates local gitignored private-skill shims under the live skill roots from ai-config-sync.private.json, so explicit private $skill invocations resolve without tracking private names or bodies in the public repo.

Codex-only command allowlist rules, pruned 2026-07-29 to generic recurring commands only (git add/commit/push/restore, curl -L, ps, emacs batch, emacsclient --eval). One-off approvals, dead-PID kills, the AGENTS.md symlink rule, and the arbitrary-command CODEX_HOME env prefix were removed; do not re-add task-specific or PID-specific rules. There is no Claude counterpart; material policy changes should be recorded here.
